utility.notes: Xcel Energy's list of Colorado communities served, dated 10/2015, shows Wheat Ridge with gas and electricity service. The list names communities, not individual addresses. The City's Renewable Energy page points residents to Xcel Energy programs such as Windsource. The City's building and sustainability pages do not name the electric utility for each address or give a way to look it up. Check the utility named on your electric bill before you apply for interconnection.

value.name: Xcel Energy
value.notes: Applies to addresses served by Xcel Energy; check your electric bill. Xcel says all solar customers receive net energy metering benefits, and any excess is held in a virtual bank to be applied against future bills.

county.notes: The City's building pages do not name the county or say how to confirm that an address is inside city limits.

permit_authority.value: City of Wheat Ridge Building Division
permit_authority.notes: The Building Division reviews plans, issues permits and completes inspections. Its office is at 7500 W. 29th Ave., 2nd Floor, Wheat Ridge, CO, and walk-in customer hours are Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. The City highly encourages appointments. The City says Wheat Ridge is not a full-service city: special districts provide fire, water and sanitation service. The City's pages do not say how to confirm that an address is inside city limits. If you are unsure whether a permit is needed, the City says to contact Building and Inspection Services at (303) 235-2855, Option 1.

permit_url.notes: As of January 2025, all permits are submitted and managed through the City's OpenGov permit portal. The City's Solar APP + page says licensed contractors can now submit through SolarAPP+ and the City of Wheat Ridge Online Permit Center. A system that is not eligible for SolarAPP+ needs a regular building permit: follow the City's Submittal Checklist, then submit the application through the Online Permit Center.

interconnection_url.notes: This applies if Xcel Energy is your electric utility; check your electric bill. Xcel says that in most cases the developer or installer submits the interconnection application on your behalf, or you can manage your own. Xcel says you can submit an interconnection application online once you understand the state, local and utility requirements and permits. Xcel highly recommends that construction of your system should not start until your application receives full approval from the Xcel Energy engineering team and all final agreements are fully signed. The process ends with a permission to operate letter from Xcel to the generator owner. Xcel's permission to operate is a separate approval from the City permit and the City's inspections.

value.name: Renewable Battery Connect
value.description: Xcel says that when you add an eligible solar charged battery to your home or small business and participate, Xcel can automatically manage your battery during periods of peak demand on the grid (load control events). Upfront incentive, General: $250 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to $5,000 per application). Income Qualified: $1,000 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). Disproportionately Impacted Community: $500 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). There is also a $100 annual participation incentive for all customer types for participating in control events (for 5 years).
value.eligibility: An Xcel Energy program for a home or small business that adds an eligible solar charged battery. Xcel says eligible equipment includes all Tesla Powerwall models or all current Enphase models. Check that Xcel is your electric utility first.

battery_programs.notes: Xcel's page shows a 2026 General incentive budget with $10,635,423 available, on figures dated 11/02/2026. The City lists a separate $170 Solar Battery Storage permit fee.

value.required_when: When you apply for the Solar App+ Permit in OpenGov, after SolarAPP+ approves the design.

value.required_when: Solar App+ Permit in OpenGov. The City's Solar APP + page calls it a "City of Brea" completed building permit application and does not name a Wheat Ridge form. Ask the Building Division which application to upload.

value.name: Items on the City's Submittal Checklist (systems not eligible for SolarAPP+)
value.required_when: Solar systems that are not eligible for SolarAPP+. The City's Solar APP + page names the Submittal Checklist but does not list its items, so ask the Building Division for the current checklist.

value.name: Copy of the fire district's online submittal confirmation (permits that need fire district review)
value.required_when: Certain permits require evidence that the project was submitted to the fire, water or sanitation district for review. West Metro Fire District and Arvada Fire District both require online submittals through their own plan review portal. The City's pages do not say whether a residential solar or battery permit needs fire district review, so ask the permit desk.

required_documents.notes: For a SolarAPP+ permit, the City's Solar APP + page asks you to provide the SolarAPP+ approval number and upload the SolarAPP+ Approval Document, a site plan, a business license and a completed building permit application. SolarAPP+ generates a checklist and a SolarAPP+ ID when it approves the design. The City's pages do not list the plan sheets for a standard solar permit.

value: SolarAPP+ path: your licensed contractor submits the solar design at SolarAPP+ for automated review, and SolarAPP+ generates a checklist and a SolarAPP+ ID when it approves the design.

Apply for the City permit in the OpenGov portal. For SolarAPP+, select Building Permits - Quick Permits, then Solar App+ Permit. A system that is not eligible for SolarAPP+ needs a regular building permit.

If Xcel Energy is your utility, your installer usually submits the interconnection application to Xcel. Xcel recommends not starting construction until the application is fully approved and all final agreements are signed.
Pay the City fees online in OpenGov. Building permit fees are payable when the permit is issued, and work should not start before the building permit is issued.
Request City inspections through the OpenGov permit portal, before 4 p.m. for a next day building inspection. A SolarAPP+ permit is scheduled the same way as other permits.
Check inspection results, including approval or corrections, in the OpenGov permit portal.
For Xcel customers: after the interconnection is approved and all contracts are signed, Xcel works with you and your contractors to witness test and energize the system.
Xcel sends a permission to operate letter to the generator owner.
inspection_steps.notes: The City's pages do not list which inspections a solar permit needs, so ask the Building Division when you schedule. AM inspections typically occur between 8 a.m. and noon, and PM inspections between noon and 3 p.m. Same day inspection requests must be received by 11 a.m. and depend on inspector availability. The City permit, the City's inspections and Xcel's permission to operate are separate approvals.

timeline_days.notes: The City's Building Permits page says review can range from 2 to 6 weeks depending on permit type and scope of work, and lists residential review as up to four weeks. The page does not give a review time specific to solar permits. Expedited plan review is not available, and plans are reviewed in the order they are received. For projects that qualify for SolarAPP+, the City's Solar APP + page describes instantaneous permit issuance once the SolarAPP+ application is completed. Building permits are valid for 180 days, and the City grants automatic 180 extensions for approved inspections that demonstrate substantial progress.

value.program_or_pathway: SolarAPP+ for qualifying residential rooftop systems, or a standard solar permit in OpenGov
other_conditions: SolarAPP+ is for licensed contractors and covers most residential, roof-mounted, retrofit photovoltaic systems.

In the City's eligibility table, residential roof-mounted systems from 1.0 to 38.4 kW (A/C) can use the State Solar Permit (SolarAPP+) if they qualify, projects that do not qualify use the Standard Solar Permit, and systems of 38.5 kW (A/C) or more need a standard permit.
Only projects that conform to the SolarAPP+ Eligibility Checklist may use the SolarAPP+ portal.
SolarAPP+ cannot currently be used for ground-mounted systems, new construction or non-residential projects (multi-family, commercial, community and utility-scale).
The City's page says SolarAPP+ does not cover PV systems interconnecting with main panel busbars exceeding 225A, or a re-roofing permit (Class A).
SolarAPP+ charges its own processing fee for plan review.
Anyone doing work for compensation on private property in Wheat Ridge must hold a current contractor license.

Electrical contractors do not need a City license but must register with the City (no fee), with the approved registration application, insurance documents and copies of their State of Colorado Master Electrician and Electrical Contractor licenses.
The City's pages do not say whether a homeowner may get a solar permit for work on their own home, so ask the Building Division.

The City's Adopted Codes page says the 2026 National Electrical Code is now in effect for all electrical permitting and inspection in the city, while the list of Building Division responsibilities still names the 2023 National Electrical Code, so confirm the edition with the Building Division.
Xcel Energy net metering: you must be an Xcel residential or business electricity customer, and the name on the application must match the name on the Xcel account or bill.

Xcel Energy net metering: the system must be sized so expected generation, combined with other distributed generation at the service address, does not exceed 200% of historical consumption (the previous 12 months at the time of application).
Xcel Energy net metering: all equipment must be UL 1741 SB certified and listed on the California Energy Commission Solar Equipment Lists.

eligibility_constraints.notes: License and registration rules are from the City's Contractor Licenses & Registration page. Conditions marked Xcel Energy are Xcel's and apply to Xcel customers.

permit_fees.notes: Fees are from the Project Specific Fees table on the City's Permit Valuation & Fees page, per the 2026 adopted budget. These flat fees exclude use tax, which is calculated based on valuation. City Code Section 22-68 requires use tax on the items, materials and equipment used in construction, and the use tax charge is 3.5% of 60% of the project valuation. SolarAPP+ also charges its own processing fee for plan review. Building permit and other applicable fees are payable at the time of permit issuance, and payments are made in the OpenGov Permit Portal. Permit fees are doubled when work is started before a building permit is obtained. For a same day inspection, the Building Inspections page says a fee of $170 will be assessed, and the 2026 fee table lists $85 per hour, minimum 2 hours. The two pages differ on the re-inspection fee: the 2026 fee table lists $85 per hour (minimum 1 hour), while the Building Inspections page says a late cancellation is subject to a $60 re-inspection fee. Confirm the re-inspection fee with the permit desk.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Income Qualified upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says customers who qualify under the terms of Income Qualified can receive an upfront rebate of $3 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer and qualify under Xcel's Income Qualified terms.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Disproportionately Impacted Communities upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says Disproportionately Impacted Communities can receive an upfront rebate of $0.50 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer. The rebate is for Disproportionately Impacted Communities.

rebates.notes: The Solar*Rewards rebates are Xcel Energy programs. Xcel's page says that as of 10/05/2026 it moved $1,050,000 from Solar*Rewards C&I to the Solar*Rewards Residential IQ/DIC program. The City's pages describe no City-funded rebate for residential solar.
